title: Signal graph definition
description: A canonical signal graph. Single source of truth for generated pseudocode and diagrams.

name.description: PascalCase graph identifier. Also the node name when the graph is used as a sub-graph in another definition.

parameters.description: Ordered list of external type signatures the graph accepts, including both data inputs and capability handles.

capabilities.description: Subset of `parameters` that are capability handles (as opposed to data inputs). Each entry must appear verbatim in `parameters`.

inputs.description: Typed inputs to the node. Entries that match strings in the enclosing graph's `capabilities` are treated as capability handles; the rest are data inputs.

output.description: Single output type, or a sum type expressed as `role1: Type1 | role2: Type2 | ...` with edge-addressable role labels.

discharges_trust.description: Set to true on nodes that consume an `Untrusted<_>` input and emit a non-`Untrusted` output. The validator requires this marker so trust discharge is explicit at the graph level.

capability_identities.description: Optional map from a capability type the node holds (an entry of `inputs` that also appears in the enclosing graph's `capabilities`) to an identity label. Names a distinct instance of that capability type: two nodes naming the same type with distinct labels bind distinct handle instances; the same label binds one shared instance. Absent, the node is provisioned by type exactly as before. This is the canonical-source spelling of the runtime's `assemble(identities=...)` argument, and on a sub-graph-reference node it routes a named instance across the composition boundary.

binds_principal.description: Set to true on nodes licensed to bind or rebind the principal on whose authority downstream work is done — the acting-on-behalf-of hop. Mirrors discharges_trust: it is the sole marker that lets a node change a propagating annotation, so delegation is visible in the graph source rather than hidden in node logic. A node declaring it must hold at least one capability; a binder with no authority to scope is a declaration with no meaning.

requires.description: Preconditions on the node's input, as a list of predicates in the closed contract vocabulary: `path <op> literal`, `path in [a, b]`, `present(path)`, `len(path) <op> integer`. A violation blames the upstream wiring that supplied the value.

ensures.description: Postconditions on the node's output, in the same vocabulary as `requires`. A violation blames the node's implementation.

from.description: Source node name, optionally with a `.role` suffix to address a specific variant of a sum-typed output.

layout.description: Optional rendering hints consumed by scripts/generate-graph.py. No semantic effect.
